learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the basics of agriculture, the different types of crops, and the essential step-by-step processes involved in farming!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Agriculture is the science and art of cultivating plants and livestock. It is the backbone of human civilization, providing food, clothing, and raw materials.
Crops are mainly divided by seasons. Kharif crops (Rice, Maize) are sown in the rainy season. Rabi crops (Wheat, Mustard) are sown in the winter season.
The first step is turning and loosening the soil (ploughing). After the soil is ready, good quality, healthy seeds are selected and planted at the right depth (sowing).
Plants need water at regular intervals (irrigation). They also need food! Farmers add manure (natural) and fertilizers (chemical) to the soil to make it nutrient-rich.
Once the crop is mature and golden, it is cut (harvesting). The grains are then safely stored in silos or granaries to protect them from moisture, rats, and insects.

fun_activity.title: 🌱 The Sprout Test
fun_activity.instructions: Take a few moong or gram seeds. Soak them in water overnight, then tie them in a wet cotton cloth. Observe them after 1-2 days. You just did the first step of farming: Germination!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Kharif (monsoon) and Rabi (winter) crops with two examples each.
📌 Memorize the sequence of agricultural practices: Soil preparation -> Sowing -> Adding manure -> Irrigation -> Harvesting -> Storage.
📌 Understand the difference between natural manure (eco-friendly) and chemical fertilizers (fast but can harm soil over time).
quick_recap: ⭐ The plough, hoe, and cultivator are traditional tools used for soil preparation.
⭐ Modern irrigation methods like Drip and Sprinkler systems help save a lot of water.
⭐ Storage is as important as growing; poor storage can ruin months of hard work.
